description:
Build the replacement release tooling that supersedes automate_release.py.
The new flow has three pieces:

1. Makefile release target: bumps version, generates changelog, opens a
   release PR. Maintainer reviews, edits changelog, squash-merges.
2. GitHub Actions release workflow: triggered by tag push, runs final
   CI, builds wheel and sdist, publishes to PyPI via trusted publisher.
3. Standalone changelog generator extracted from automate_release.py,
   keeping the Claude-summarisation fallback.

automate_release.py and the rest of the old machinery still exist during
this phase as a fallback. They are deleted in Phase 6.

Under Option B, these artefacts are added on private (current dev locus)
and land on public via the Phase 4 final sync. The Makefile target uses
`origin` from the start; when invoked from the public clone post-Phase 5,
origin is the canonical repo. Do NOT invoke `make release` from the
private clone — its `origin` remote does not exist (private has `private`
and `public` remotes today).

Plan file: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/single-repo-migration.md (Phase 3).

anti_patterns.dont: bake secrets or tokens into release.yml
anti_patterns.why: trusted publisher uses OIDC and needs no static tokens; if you find yourself reaching for a PYPI_API_TOKEN, you are doing it wrong.

anti_patterns.dont: publish to real PyPI from a sandbox/test workflow run
anti_patterns.why: PyPI rejects re-uploads of the same version; a botched test burns the version number forever.
reproducible builds were the one piece of the old apparatus worth keeping (D7); computing it from the tag commit preserves that property cheaply.

preserves.behavior: The PyPI trusted-publisher configuration remains unchanged - the new workflow uses the same publisher as the old one would have.
automate_release.py and friends still work end-to-end during this phase. The new flow runs alongside, not in place of, the old one.
update_version.py is reused as-is, not duplicated.

verifications.description: scripts/generate_changelog_entry.py exists and is importable as a CLI
.github/workflows/release.yml exists and triggers on tag push
Sandbox dry-run produces a release PR

work_units.notes:
Lift functions automate_release.py:_build_raw_changelog,
_summarize_changelog_with_claude, and generate_changelog_entry
(lines 156-414) into a standalone script with its own argparse.
Args: --version, --release-date, --since-tag (optional, defaults
to most recent v* tag), --output (default CHANGELOG.md).
Keep the Claude CLI summarisation fallback exactly as-is. Reuse
update_version.py for version bumping (do not duplicate).

Append to Makefile:
  release:
      @test -n "$(VERSION)" || (echo "Usage: make release VERSION=X.Y.Z" && exit 1)
      uv run python scripts/update_version.py --version $(VERSION)
      uv run python scripts/generate_changelog_entry.py --version $(VERSION)
      git checkout -b release/v$(VERSION)
      git add CHANGELOG.md benchbox/__init__.py pyproject.toml docs/ landing/ benchbox/_metadata.py 2>/dev/null || true
      git commit -m "Release v$(VERSION)"
      git push origin release/v$(VERSION)
      gh pr create --title "Release v$(VERSION)" --body-file .github/RELEASE_PR_TEMPLATE.md
Note: under Option B, `origin` is the canonical remote in the public
clone (~/Developer/benchbox-public). The Makefile is intended to run
from there post-Phase 5. Add a comment in the Makefile explaining
this so it is not invoked accidentally from the private clone before
dev-locus migration.

Short template with a checklist:
  ## Release vX.Y.Z
  - [ ] Reviewed the auto-generated changelog
  - [ ] Edited any unclear bullets
  - [ ] Confirmed version bump in benchbox/__init__.py, pyproject.toml,
        docs/index.rst landing pages
  After merge: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z. The
  release.yml workflow handles the rest.

Triggers: push tags v*.
Jobs:
  - checkout with fetch-depth 0 (need history for SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH)
  - setup uv (astral-sh/setup-uv@v3)
  - compute SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the tag's commit timestamp:
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct ${GITHUB_REF_NAME})" >> $GITHUB_ENV
  - run final pytest -m fast as a sanity check
  - uv run python -m build
  - verify the wheel: pip install dist/*.whl in a fresh venv,
    assert benchbox.__version__ == GITHUB_REF_NAME without v prefix
  - publish via pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
    (trusted publisher already configured per CHANGELOG)
Permissions: id-token: write (PyPI), contents: read.

work_units.notes:
Optional. Under Option B, the new flow gets exercised on real public
main in Phase 4; most issues will surface there. Skip this work unit
if you would rather catch issues during the actual v0.3.0 cut and
iterate.
If running:
  git checkout -b sandbox-release-flow
  make release VERSION=0.0.0-test
  Review the resulting PR. Close without merging. No PyPI publish
  because no tag was pushed.
Note: requires a public clone with origin set, since the Makefile
pushes to origin. From private clone this will fail.
